subLocations.name: sorcerous sundries
subLocations.lore:
History
While Sorcerous Sundries was established as a store for the arcane, for many years the building was used as a private residence, a restaurant, a variety of specialty shops, and even a greenhouse.[2]

Sometime during the 15th century DR, Rivalen Blackhand re-founded the store as a shop catering to spellcasters, specializing in Material components. However, he denied having magic items for sale and outright refused to sell spell scrolls.

subLocations.name: Water Queen's House
subLocations.lore: A temple dedicated to [[Umberlee]], the Bitch Queen – the city's oldest temple.

subLocations.name: High House of Wonders
subLocations.lore: A grand temple to [[Gond]] Wondermaker that consisted of numerous expansive workshops within which the [[Gondar]] [[priest]]s created experimental devices and machinations for the Baldurian people.

subLocations.name: Lady's Hall
subLocations.lore: A prosperous temple of [[Tymora]], the Lady Luck, built soon after the founding of [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Watchful Shield
subLocations.lore: A shrine of [[Helm]] the Vigilant, located in the [[Manorborn]] district of [[Baldur's Gate]] within a diminutive chapel with wings extending from either side of its front doorway, and the [[silver]] eye of Helm inscribed above.

subLocations.name: Shrine of the Suffering
subLocations.lore: A shrine of [[Ilmater]], the Maimed God, established before [[1358 DR]] that served as a soup kitchen in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Unrolling Scroll
subLocations.lore: A white [[marble]] building with a red roof and [[gold]] leaf trim – a shrine to [[Oghma]], the Patron of all Bards.

subLocations.name: Hall of Wonders
subLocations.lore: A museum in [[Baldur's Gate]] that displayed both the pragmatic and fantastical "holy relics" of the [[Church of Gond]].

subLocations.name: Church of Last Hope
subLocations.lore: A sanctuary not dedicated to any particular faith that offered shelter to the despondent, depressed, and hopeless wretches of the city and beyond.

subLocations.name: Dusthawk Hill
subLocations.lore: A tall, yellow [[granite]] steep-faced hill east of the city walls.

subLocations.name: Riverveins
subLocations.lore: A collection of subterranean mostly submerged tunnels that mazed and drained into subterranean aquifers.

subLocations.name: Rose Portal
subLocations.lore: A stone building with rose-colored windows that held the shrine dedicated to [[Lathander]] that somewhat falled out of favour by the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: The Fool's Altar
subLocations.lore: A shrine dedicated to [[Finder Wyvernspur]], the Nameless Bard, next-door to [[Ascloakan's Fine Inn]]; the shrine was supervised by the [[saurial]] [[priest]] named [[Aszloakh the Hooded]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Manycoins House
subLocations.lore: The office of the [[Merchant's League]] – a four-storied temple dedicated to [[Waukeen]] that offered mercantile services, short-term lodgings, and priestly services.
